items.title: Type the new words
items.intro: Read the English and type the Samoan. The keys under the box add the long vowels and the glottal stop.

items.why: *Alu* stays *alu* whether the going is past, present, or still to come.
As in *Sā ia fāgota.* (She went fishing.)

items.hint: A preverbal pronoun: it stands before the verb.
items.why: Between the particle and the verb sits the word for who did it: *Sā ʻou alu.* (I went.)
Swap *ʻou* for *ia* and the same things are said about someone else: *Sā ia alu.* (She went.)
A word to carry: it names a feeling rather than an action, and is used fully later in this book.
You can use it on its own from your very first day.
